### Initialize project and install dependencies

mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
pnpm add hono hono-alibaba-cloud-fc3-adapter
pnpm add -D @serverless-devs/s esbuild
mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
bun add hono hono-alibaba-cloud-fc3-adapter
bun add -D esbuild @serverless-devs/s
mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

### Initialize a Hono app with the CLI

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/agents/cli.md

Use `hono init` to add a Hono app from a create-hono template to an existing project where `npm create hono` cannot be used. The `--template` flag selects the template and `--install` installs dependencies using the package manager from the lockfile or the command that started `hono`. Without `--template`, the template is detected from files in the directory; without a terminal, the error lists the templates.

```sh
npm install -D @hono/cli
npx hono init --template cloudflare-workers --install
npx hono request /
```

### Create a basic Hono server in main.ts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/deno.md

Define a root route handler returning text and start the HTTP server using Deno.serve with app.fetch.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Deno!'))

Deno.serve(app.fetch)
```

### Initialize WebAssembly Hono project and install dependencies

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/webassembly-wasi.md

Initializes a new project directory and installs Hono alongside Bytecode Alliance WASI tools and Rolldown. Ensure that `type` is set to `"module"` in `package.json`.

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
npm i hono
npm i -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
npm i -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
yarn add hono
yarn add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
yarn add -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
pnpm init --init-type module
pnpm add hono
pnpm add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
pnpm add -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
bun add hono
bun add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
```

### Create a basic Hello World Hono application

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/basic.md

Define a starter Hono application in src/index.ts with a GET endpoint returning plain text.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => {
  return c.text('Hello Hono!')
})

export default app
```

--------------------------------

### Plugin to filter only GET requests

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/ssg.md

Example plugin using beforeRequestHook to allow only GET requests; other methods return false to skip the route.

```ts
const getOnlyPlugin: SSGPlugin = {
  beforeRequestHook: (req) => {
    if (req.method === 'GET') {
      return req
    }
    return false
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### Set, Get, and Delete Regular Cookies with setCookie, getCookie, deleteCookie

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/cookie.md

Use setCookie to set a cookie, getCookie to retrieve a specific cookie or all cookies, and deleteCookie to remove a cookie. The example shows setting a cookie, getting it by name, deleting it, and getting all cookies.

```ts
app.get('/cookie', (c) => {
  setCookie(c, 'cookie_name', 'cookie_value')
  const yummyCookie = getCookie(c, 'cookie_name')
  deleteCookie(c, 'cookie_name')
  const allCookies = getCookie(c)
  // ...
})
```

### Define REST API routes for GET and POST /posts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md

Example application providing a REST API with GET /posts returning text and POST /posts returning JSON with a custom header. Use this as the app under test.

```ts
app.get('/posts', (c) => {
  return c.text('Many posts')
})

app.post('/posts', (c) => {
  return c.json(
    {
      message: 'Created',
    },
    201,
    {
      'X-Custom': 'Thank you',
    }
  )
})
```

### Directory structure for static file serving example

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/bun.md

The directory structure that works with the `serveStatic` example above.

```text
./
├── favicon.ico
├── src
└── static
    ├── demo
    │   └── index.html
    ├── fallback.txt
    ├── hello.txt
    └── images
        └── dinotocat.png
```

--------------------------------

### List Matched Routes Including Middleware with matchedRoutes

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

matchedRoutes(c) returns all matched routes including middleware; the example shows an ALL middleware route and a GET route both appearing in the result.

```ts
app.all('/api/*', (c, next) => {
  console.log('API middleware')
  return next()
})

app.get('/api/users/:id', (c) => {
  const routes = matchedRoutes(c)
  // Returns: [
  //   { method: 'ALL', path: '/api/*', handler: [Function] },
  //   { method: 'GET', path: '/api/users/:id', handler: [Function] }
  // ]
  return c.json({ routes: routes.length })
})
```

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/examples/prisma.md

```

--------------------------------

### Create a Hello World application with fire()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/fastly.md

Defines a basic Fastly Compute entry point in src/index.ts using fire from @fastly/hono-fastly-compute. Use Hono from 'hono' rather than 'hono/quick' because fire builds router data during initialization.

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { fire } from '@fastly/hono-fastly-compute'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Fastly!'))

fire(app)
```

### Initialize project using offline cache

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/create-hono.md

Uses local template cache instead of fetching remote templates, useful for offline environments or deterministic local setups.

```bash
pnpm create hono@latest my-app --template deno --offline
```

--------------------------------

### Get request method with c.req.method

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Access the HTTP method name via c.req.method. For a GET /about/me route, the value is `GET`.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/about/me', async (c) => {
  const method = c.req.method // `GET`
  // ...
})
```

### Initialize CDK project with package manager

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/lambda-edge.md

Initialize a TypeScript CDK application and install dependencies for Hono and @hono/lambda-edge using your preferred package manager.

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
cdk init app -l typescript
npm i hono @hono/lambda-edge
mkdir lambda
```

```sh

### startTime(c, name)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Starts a timer for measuring the duration of a specific operation.

```APIDOC
### Description
Starts a performance timer under a given metric name for the current request context.

### Signature
`startTime(c, name)`

### Parameters
- **c** (Context) - Required - The Hono request context.
- **name** (string) - Required - Name identifier for the timer.

### Example
```ts
startTime(c, 'db')
const data = await db.findMany(...)
endTime(c, 'db')
```
```

### Get querystring parameters with c.req.query()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Use c.req.query('q') to get a single querystring parameter, or c.req.query() to get all params at once. The route must define the parameter in its path.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
// Query params
app.get('/search', async (c) => {
  const query = c.req.query('q')
  //     ^?
})

// Get all params at once
app.get('/search', async (c) => {
  const { q, limit, offset } = c.req.query()
  //      ^?
})
```

### Get path parameters with c.req.param()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Use c.req.param('id') to get a single path parameter, or c.req.param() to get all params at once. The route must define the parameter in its path.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
// Captured params
app.get('/entry/:id', async (c) => {
  const id = c.req.param('id')
  //    ^?
  // ...
})

// Get all params at once
app.get('/entry/:id/comment/:commentId', async (c) => {
  const { id, commentId } = c.req.param()
  //      ^?
})
```

### Get Basic Route Information with routePath and matchedRoutes

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Use routePath(c) to get the current route pattern and matchedRoutes(c) to get an array of matched routes inside a handler.

```ts
const app = new Hono()

app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  const currentPath = routePath(c) // '/posts/:id'
  const routes = matchedRoutes(c) // Array of matched routes

  return c.json({
    path: currentPath,
    totalRoutes: routes.length,
  })
})
```

```bash
supabase start # start the supabase stack

```

### Define basic routes and HTTP method handlers

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/routing.md

Demonstrates routing by HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, QUERY), wildcard paths, handling all methods with app.all, custom HTTP methods, and handling multiple methods or paths with app.on.

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
// HTTP Methods
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('GET /'))
app.post('/', (c) => c.text('POST /'))
app.put('/', (c) => c.text('PUT /'))
app.delete('/', (c) => c.text('DELETE /'))
app.query('/', (c) => c.text('QUERY /'))

// Wildcard
app.get('/wild/*/card', (c) => {
  return c.text('GET /wild/*/card')
})

// Any HTTP methods
app.all('/hello', (c) => c.text('Any Method /hello'))

// Custom HTTP method
app.on('PURGE', '/cache', (c) => c.text('PURGE Method /cache'))

// Multiple Method
app.on(['PUT', 'DELETE'], '/post', (c) =>
  c.text('PUT or DELETE /post')
)

// Multiple Paths
app.on('GET', ['/hello', '/ja/hello', '/en/hello'], (c) =>
  c.text('Hello')
)
```

### Sitemap plugin example

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/ssg.md

Advanced plugin that generates a sitemap.xml file using afterGenerateHook. It uses DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR and writes the sitemap to the output directory.

```ts
// plugins.ts
import fs from 'node:fs/promises'
import path from 'node:path'
import type { SSGPlugin } from 'hono/ssg'
import { DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR } from 'hono/ssg'

export const sitemapPlugin = (baseURL: string): SSGPlugin => {
  return {
    afterGenerateHook: (result, fsModule, options) => {
      const outputDir = options?.dir ?? DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR
      const filePath = path.join(outputDir, 'sitemap.xml')
      const urls = result.files.map((file) =>
        new URL(file, baseURL).toString()
      )
      const siteMapText = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
${urls.map((url) => `<url><loc>${url}</loc></url>`).join('\n')}
</urlset>`
      fsModule.writeFile(filePath, siteMapText)
    },
  }
}
```

### Apply multiple plugins with toSSG

})

### Redirect GET requests with trimTrailingSlash

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/trailing-slash.md

Trims trailing slashes from URLs on GET requests when the response status is 404.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { trimTrailingSlash } from 'hono/trailing-slash'

const app = new Hono({ strict: true })

app.use(trimTrailingSlash())
app.get('/about/me', (c) => c.text('Without Trailing Slash'))
```

### Enable compressed static assets with precompressed

  })
)

### Use Server-Timing middleware with metrics and timers

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Demonstrates applying the `timing` middleware to a Hono app, recording string and numeric metrics with `setMetric`, and measuring execution durations with `startTime`/`endTime` or `wrapTime`.

```js
// Specify the variable types to infer the `c.get('metric')`:
type Variables = TimingVariables

const app = new Hono<{ Variables: Variables }>()

// add the middleware to your router
app.use(timing());

app.get('/', async (c) => {

  // add custom metrics
  setMetric(c, 'region', 'europe-west3')

  // add custom metrics with timing, must be in milliseconds
  setMetric(c, 'custom', 23.8, 'My custom Metric')

  // start a new timer
  startTime(c, 'db');
  const data = await db.findMany(...);

  // end the timer
  endTime(c, 'db');

  // ...or you can also just wrap a Promise using this function:
  const data = await wrapTime(c, 'db', db.findMany(...));

  return c.json({ response: data });
});
```

### Get request pathname with c.req.path

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Access the request pathname via c.req.path. For a GET /about/me route, the value is `/about/me`.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/about/me', async (c) => {
  const pathname = c.req.path // `/about/me`
  // ...
})
```

### Example JSON output from hono routes

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/agents/cli.md

Example of the JSON output printed by hono routes, showing the router and resolved routes.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "router": "SmartRouter + RegExpRouter",
    "routes": [
      {
        "method": "GET",
        "path": "/",
        "name": "[handler]",
        "isMiddleware": false
      },
      {
        "method": "POST",
        "path": "/posts",
        "name": "[handler]",
        "isMiddleware": false
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```sh

```

--------------------------------

### Test GET /posts with app.request

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md

Make a GET request to /posts and assert the status is 200 and the text response is 'Many posts'.

```ts
describe('Example', () => {
  test('GET /posts', async () => {
    const res = await app.request('/posts')
    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
    expect(await res.text()).toBe('Many posts')
  })
})
```

### Install Hono Skills with skills.sh or GitHub CLI

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/agents/index.md

Installs the hono and hono-jsx Agent Skills. Both methods place the skills where your agent reads them.

```sh
# skills.sh
npx skills add honojs/skills

# GitHub CLI
gh skill install honojs/skills hono
gh skill install honojs/skills hono-jsx
```

Use the bun package manager to scaffold a new Hono project. Select the `nodejs` template when prompted.

```sh
bun create hono@latest my-app
```

### Get request URL with c.req.url

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Access the full request URL string via c.req.url. For a GET /about/me route, the value is `http://localhost:8787/about/me`.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/about/me', async (c) => {
  const url = c.req.url // `http://localhost:8787/about/me`
  // ...
})
```

--------------------------------

### Test GET request with app.request

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/hono.md

Use app.request to send a GET request by pathname and assert the response status. The app returns a Response object.

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
declare const test: (name: string, fn: () => void) => void
declare const expect: (value: any) => any
// ---cut---
test('GET /hello is ok', async () => {
  const res = await app.request('/hello')
  expect(res.status).toBe(200)
})
```

### Deploying a minified application using PatternRouter

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/concepts/routers.md

Shows output from deploying a minified Hono application with PatternRouter via Wrangler. PatternRouter produces compact build outputs under 15KB for environments with strict resource constraints.

```console
$ npx wrangler deploy --minify ./src/index.ts
 ⛅️ wrangler 3.20.0
-------------------
Total Upload: 14.68 KiB / gzip: 5.38 KiB
```

### Get request header value with c.req.header()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Use c.req.header('User-Agent') to get a specific request header value. When called with no arguments, all keys in the returned record are lowercase.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/', (c) => {
  const userAgent = c.req.header('User-Agent')
  //      ^?
  return c.text(`Your user agent is ${userAgent}`)
})
```

--------------------------------

### Import Context Storage Middleware and helpers

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/context-storage.md

Import contextStorage, getContext, and tryGetContext helper functions from hono/context-storage.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import {
  contextStorage,
  getContext,
  tryGetContext,
} from 'hono/context-storage'
```

--------------------------------

### Get multiple querystring parameter values with c.req.queries()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Use c.req.queries('tags') to get multiple values for the same querystring parameter, e.g. /search?tags=A&tags=B. The result is a string array.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/search', async (c) => {
  // tags will be string[]
  const tags = c.req.queries('tags')
  //     ^?
  // ...
})
```

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/google-cloud-run.md

```sh
gcloud projects create --set-as-default --name="my app"
```

--------------------------------

### Hello World Hono app for Bun

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/bun.md

A minimal Hono app that responds with 'Hello Bun!' at the root path. When setting up on an existing project, place this script in `src/index.ts` as expected by `bun run dev`.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Bun!'))

export default app
```

--------------------------------

### Create Prisma client helper in lib/prisma.ts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/examples/prisma.md

Initializes a reusable PrismaClient instance configured with the PrismaD1 adapter using the D1 binding.

```ts
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
import { PrismaD1 } from '@prisma/adapter-d1'

const prismaClients = {
  async fetch(db: D1Database) {
    const adapter = new PrismaD1(db)
    const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter })
    return prisma
  },
}

export default prismaClients
```

--------------------------------

### endTime(c, name)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Stops a previously started timer and records the duration in the metrics.

```APIDOC
### Description
Stops an active timer identified by name and calculates the elapsed duration for the Server-Timing header.

### Signature
`endTime(c, name)`

### Parameters
- **c** (Context) - Required - The Hono request context.
- **name** (string) - Required - Name identifier for the timer that was started.

### Example
```ts
startTime(c, 'db')
const data = await db.findMany(...)
endTime(c, 'db')
```
```

### Configure Alibaba Cloud credentials with Serverless Devs

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/ali-function-compute.md

Runs the Serverless Devs interactive configuration command to set up your Alibaba Cloud AccessKeyID and AccessKeySecret.

```sh
npx s config add
# Please select a provider: Alibaba Cloud (alibaba)
# Input your AccessKeyID & AccessKeySecret
```
